title: How to properly Market an AI Coded Game.
author: Emergency-Film-3190
selftext: ive been working on a game for some months now, not rreally one of those one promt games ive been actually putting time into working on art and stuff, the only thing im not doing myself is coding ive been using a mix of gpt and small amount of codex. Are people still mad about using ai for code? i feel like its not safe to even show the game cuz i dont want the AI Slop label. all the art was made by me or i used free assets for placeholders from Itch io. sounds all from online free sources. Just me and openai for help or coding lol. Anyways How do i put it out here in the world? Will it not preform well cuz i used AI to code?

comments.author: frigginwizard420
comments.body:
With increasing frequency successful games are admitting to AI use, and the anti AI "this is slop" commenters are so overplayed that even they are getting tired of it.

Just do what you want, and be transparent about it. The world is changing.   

Slop is the quality of the content, not how you made it, and dont let anyone tell you different.

replies.author: sanguilarity
replies.body: The irony of the slop commenters is that they are mostly regurgitating comments they saw other people make

comments.author: niloony
comments.body: It's always scary to present your work. The AI stuff is irrelevant, people are jerks either way and they were jerks to indie devs before AI. Though you should listen if everyone says it sucks or ignores it. You must put your game out there to test it.

comments.author: Arkenhammer
comments.body:
Marketing begins with a competitive analysis before you start making the game. Figure out what players in your genre are looking for and where they find games. Make a game that fills a gap in the market—either higher quality than what’s out there or innovative in a way that is appealing. 

Generally I start my marketing effort by finding YouTube and Twitch streamers who cover similar games and figure out a pitch for why it would be good for their channel to cover my game. I’ll build the game with that pitch in mind.

comments.author: Riolutail
comments.body:
Brick by brick unfortunately - reach out to cc’s knowing its extremely marginal returns (but you just need one). Start and manage socials, etc. Ai can help u code but it wont help u generate a playerbase/community. Thats something you have to work hard for or like someone else said, hire out to someone who actually has marketing skills or pay for ads/promotions on socials.

And slop is tied to quality, not whether you used AI. Its much easier to put out bad quality / non-unique content because of AI, but just take the time to make your game look good and actually fun to play. My best recommendation is to ditch the placeholder art if it isnt coherent or has character asap cuz thats the fastest way to get a slop label slapped on your game, no matter how much time and effort went into game design and mechanics. 

 There are no shortcuts to success - good luck

replies.author: Emergency-Film-3190
replies.body: my placeholder art is just a quicky i made up no ai or nuomthin just not finished, most gets done as i make it tho

replies.author: Riolutail
replies.body: then that's probably fine, as long as theres no more placeholder stuff by the time you demo. And note non-ai art can still be slop too again depending on effort and perceived quality, so just make sure the art you do end up using looks good and coherent
